historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah - Volume 8, Page 237 The name Samit carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: A battle between Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan. Muawiya sent a man named Samit ibn Jabalah Al-Asadi to Ali, who deceitfully proposed that he would defect from Muawiya's camp and join Ali. However, after Ali accepted Samit and gave him a position in his army, Samit betrayed him by informing Muawiya of Ali's movements and plans.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf - Page 539 The name Samit carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: A group of rebels, led by a man named Musaylimah ibn Habib Al-Hanafi, revolted against Ali ibn Abi Talib, claiming prophethood for himself. Ali sent an army under the command of Abd Allah ibn Awsaja Al-Asadi to deal with the rebels. During the campaign, a man named Samit ibn Jabalah Al-Asadi joined Musaylimah's side, but was later captured and executed by Abd Allah.
